subtitle: Across the sea, a collateral child-king saves a crumbling Pallava throne

panels.action: Young Nandivarman II Pallavamalla stands in full Pallava regalia on a Kanchipuram temple terrace, stone lions at his side and the city stretching behind him under a glowing southern sky.

dialogue.text: In the age when Pallava Kanchipuram trembled without an heir, a boy from distant Kambuja crossed the sea to be crowned Nandivarman II Pallavamalla.

i18n.hi: जब उत्तराधिकारी बिना कांप रहा था पल्लव कांचीपुरम, दूर कम्बुज से एक बालक समुद्र लांघकर आया, नंदिवर्मन द्वितीय पल्लवमल्ला बनकर ताज पहनने.

panels.action: A grand aerial view of Kanchipuram in the early eighth century, temple towers rising among dusty streets, with one royal palace courtyard ominously quiet under a hazy sun.

dialogue.text: Around 731 CE, the Pallava capital Kanchipuram lay heavy in silence. Paramesvaravarman II was dead, and no son stepped forward to claim his lion throne.

i18n.hi: लगभग ७३१ ईसवी में, पल्लव राजधानी कांचीपुरम पर सन्नाटा भारी था। परमेश्वरवर्मन द्वितीय मर चुका था, और कोई पुत्र सिंहासन पर चढ़ने आगे नहीं आया था।

panels.action: Inside a dim stone hall, worried ministers and generals sit in council around an empty, ornate throne, their faces tense, scrolls and palm-leaf records scattered before them.

dialogue.text: In the council hall, elders of the Pallava court stared at the vacant seat. Succession had broken; the line of royal fathers and sons could no longer simply continue.

i18n.hi: सभा-गृह में पल्लव दरबार के बुज़ुर्ग खाली सिंहासन को घूरते रहे। उत्तराधिकार की कड़ी टूट गई थी; राजपुत्रों की परंपरा अब सीधे आगे नहीं बढ़ सकती थी।

panels.action: A learned court scholar unrolls a long copper plate genealogy before the gathered nobles, the gleam of the plates catching lamplight, while others lean in to read.

dialogue.text: They turned to written memory. Copper plates and palm leaves recalled Pallava ancestors, collateral branches and distant kin, seeking a thread that could be knotted back to the crown.

i18n.hi: उन्होंने लिखी हुई यादों का सहारा लिया। ताम्रपत्र और ताड़पत्रों पर दर्ज पल्लव पुरखे, सगी-सहोदर शाखाएँ और दूर के रिश्ते खोजे गए, ताकि राजमुकुट से फिर जुड़ सके कोई धागा।

panels.action: A hand points on an engraved copper plate to an inscription line mentioning a Pallava prince tied to Kambujadesa, the letters clear and formal in early script.

dialogue.text: Among careful lines of script, a name and place were marked: a Pallava of a collateral branch, linked to Kambujadesa, a region remembered as across the eastern waters.

i18n.hi: लिपि की सधी हुई पंक्तियों के बीच एक नाम और ठिकाना उभरा — एक सगा पल्लव, कम्बुजदेश से जुड़ा, पूर्वी जलधि पार के प्रदेश की याद दिलाता।

panels.action: A Pallava ship with high curved prow sets out from a Tamil port, sails billowing, envoys standing at the bow looking toward the misty horizon over the sea.

dialogue.text: Envoys were sent by ship, over restless waves. The plates spoke of Kambujadesa, but not its exact shore; the mission rode more on trust in lineage than on clear maps.

i18n.hi: दूत जहाज़ों से भेजे गए, उचाट लहरों पर सवार। लेखों में कम्बुजदेश का ज़िक्र था, मगर किनारा साफ़ नहीं; यह यात्रा नक्शे से ज़्यादा कुल पर भरोसे पर निकली।

panels.action: In a modest foreign courtyard, twelve-year-old Pallavamalla sits cross-legged, absorbed in a palm-leaf manuscript, simple ornaments on his neck and a calm, thoughtful face.

dialogue.text: Far from Kanchipuram lived a boy of that branch. Around twelve, called Pallavamalla, he grew under different skies, yet carried Pallava blood and stories of the southern throne.

i18n.hi: कांचीपुरम से बहुत दूर, उसी शाखा का एक बालक रहता था। लगभग बारह साल का, पल्लवमल्ला कहलाता, अलग आसमानों तले बड़ा होता, पर नसों में पल्लव रक्त और दक्षिण के सिंहासन की कथाएँ लिए।

panels.action: Pallava envoys in fine but travel-worn garments stand before the young Pallavamalla, one gesturing toward a simple throne-like seat as the boy looks up, startled yet steady.

dialogue.text: “Prince, the lion seat of Kanchipuram waits. Will you answer its call?”

i18n.hi: “राजकुमार, कांचीपुरम का सिंहासन तुम्हें पुकार रहा है। क्या तुम इसका उत्तर दोगे?”

panels.action: A close view of Pallavamalla's face as he gazes toward the distant sea, eyes reflecting both fear and resolve, evening light touching his features.

dialogue.text: “From this quiet court to a great kingdom… Can a boy bear such weight?”

i18n.hi: “इस शांत दरबार से एक महा राज्य तक… क्या इतना भार एक बालक उठा सकता है?”

panels.action: The boy stands on the deck of a ship bound west, holding the railing, hair whipped by the sea wind, with envoys behind him and the sun low over the waves.

dialogue.text: He agreed, and the sea carried him toward an unknown city that would become his world. A child sailed to mend an adult kingdom’s broken line.

i18n.hi: उसने हामी भरी, और समुद्र उसे एक अनजानी नगरी की ओर ले चला, जो आगे चलकर उसका जग बननी थी। एक बच्चा जहाज़ पर चढ़ा, टूटी राजलाइन जोड़ने।

panels.action: The ship arrives at a bustling Kanchipuram river landing, with crowds, traders and temple spires beyond, as Pallavamalla steps onto Tamil soil for the first time.

dialogue.text: Kanchipuram rose before him: crowded streets, the towers of many shrines, the weight of Pallava history pressing from every stone as the foreign-born prince stepped ashore.

i18n.hi: कांचीपुरम उसके आगे उठा: भीड़ भरी गलियाँ, अनेकों मंदिरों के शिखर, हर पत्थर से टपकता पल्लव इतिहास, जैसे ही विदेश-जन्मा राजकुमार किनारे उतरा।

panels.action: Within a palace hall, elders examine the boy formally, measuring his posture and listening as he recites his lineage, while he stands composed in simple attire.

dialogue.text: Ministers tested him. He spoke his ancestors, learned the ways of the court, and showed that, though young, he could carry the name that bound them all together.

i18n.hi: मंत्री उसे परखने लगे। उसने अपने पुरखों का वंश सुनाया, दरबार के तौर-तरीके सीखे, और दिखा दिया कि कम उम्र के बावजूद वह वह नाम उठा सकता है जो सबको जोड़ता है।

panels.action: In a packed coronation hall, Pallavamalla sits on the lion throne, freshly anointed, garlanded and crowned, while nobles and priests stand in ordered rows around him.

dialogue.text: In that hall, they transformed him. The boy from Kambuja was crowned as Nandivarman II Pallavamalla, joining collateral blood to the central Pallava line in a single ritual act.

i18n.hi: उसी सभा में उसका रूप बदला। कम्बुजा का वह बालक नंदिवर्मन द्वितीय पल्लवमल्ला बना, एक ही राजकर्म में सगी शाखा का रक्त मुख्य पल्लव वंश से जोड़ दिया गया।

panels.action: An early view of the Vaikunta Perumal temple under construction, scaffolding around its rising stone tiers, as Nandivarman II looks up, imagining its future.

dialogue.text: Years into his reign, Nandivarman II ordered a new kind of monument: the Vaikunta Perumal temple, a stone palace for Vishnu and a quiet record of kings.

i18n.hi: राज के कुछ ही वर्षों में नंदिवर्मन द्वितीय ने एक नए तरह का स्मारक बनवाया — वैकुण्ठ पेरुमाल मंदिर, विष्णु का पत्थर-महल और राजाओं की शांत कथा।

panels.action: Inside the temple cloister, sculptors carve relief panels of Pallava kings and the boy’s coronation, while Nandivarman II watches, hand resting on a pillar.

dialogue.text: On its walls, artisans etched the story of Pallava rulers and his own chosen rise, turning royal memory into stone, one of India’s rare early dynastic autobiographies.

i18n.hi: उसकी दीवारों पर शिल्पियों ने पल्लव नरेशों की गाथा और उसके चुने हुए उदय को उकेरा, राज-स्मृति को पत्थर में बदलते हुए — भारत की विरल आरंभिक राजवंशी आत्मकथाओं में एक।

panels.action: Nandivarman II stands alone in the temple’s inner passage, facing a relief of his youthful coronation, the dim lamplight soft on his older, reflective face.

dialogue.text: “Let future eyes see how a kingdom chose, and how I answered.”

i18n.hi: “आने वाली आँखें देखें, कैसे एक राज्य ने चुना, और मैंने कैसे उत्तर दिया।”

panels.action: Devotees circle around Vaikunta Perumal temple, priests leading processions, as the king watches from a terrace, the temple now woven into the city’s daily rhythms.

dialogue.text: Under him, temples like Vaikunta Perumal bound royal power to devotion. Bhakti songs and political memory met in stone, giving his reign both sacred and civic shape.

i18n.hi: उसके राज में वैकुण्ठ पेरुमाल जैसे मंदिरों ने राजशक्ति को भक्ति से बाँधा। भक्ति गीत और शासन की यादें पत्थर में मिलीं, उसके राज को एक साथ पवित्र और सार्वजनिक रूप दिया।

panels.action: An older Nandivarman II sits quietly with copper plates before him, inscribed with grants and his genealogy, his hand resting gently on the metal.

dialogue.text: He reigned for decades, issuing land grants and affirming his place in the Pallava order, not by claiming divine ancestry, but by recording human choices in careful inscriptions.

i18n.hi: वह दशकों तक राज करता रहा, भूमि दान करता, और पल्लव व्यवस्था में अपनी जगह पक्की करता — देव-वंश का दावा नहीं, बल्कि मनुष्यों के फैसलों को सधे हुए अभिलेखों में दर्ज कर के।

panels.action: A close, timeless view of the Vaikunta Perumal relief showing envoys, the sea journey, and the boy king’s coronation, carved faces lit by a shaft of natural light.

dialogue.text: The panels still speak: when a royal line faltered, Pallava institutions bent, not broke, choosing a distant child and making him king—proving that legitimacy can endure when a community can renew itself.

i18n.hi: पट्ट चित्र आज भी कहते हैं: जब राजवंश लड़खड़ाया, पल्लव संस्थाएँ झुकीं पर टूटी नहीं; उन्होंने दूर के बालक को चुना और राजा बनाया — साबित करते हुए कि वैधता बची रहती है, जब समाज खुद को फिर से गढ़ सके।

title_i18n.en: The Boy from Kambuja Crowned at Kanchi
title_i18n.hi: कम्बुजा का बालक, कांची में ताजपोशी

subtitle_i18n.en: Across the sea, a collateral child-king saves a crumbling Pallava throne
subtitle_i18n.hi: समंदर पार से आया सगा बाल-राजा, बचाता ढहता पल्लव सिंहासन
